evals.name: plain-pytorch-near-miss
evals.prompt: Read-only review: in plain PyTorch, does torch.nn.Dropout(p=0.2) need a wrapper to operate on one tensor? Give a tiny standard PyTorch example and explain train/eval behavior. There is no NexuML integration in this task. Do not read project files, write anything or execute code.
evals.expected_output: Answers with standard PyTorch without loading unrelated NexuML skills.
expectations: Does not load any NexuML skill for the plain PyTorch near-miss.
Explains ordinary dropout and training/evaluation behavior without inventing NexuML requirements.

evals.name: paper-summary-near-miss
evals.prompt: Read-only explanation: distinguish a resource paper describing procedural agent skills from a controlled experiment measuring whether skills improve agent performance. Which evidence would establish the latter? This is conceptual paper interpretation, not an implementation, paper reproduction or NexuML experiment. No file reads, tools, code or execution needed.
evals.expected_output: Explains evidence limitations without loading NexuML reproduction/research skills.
expectations: Does not load any NexuML skill for conceptual paper interpretation.
Distinguishes documentation/resource measurements from matched task-level efficacy evidence.

evals.name: framework-contributor-near-miss
evals.prompt: Read-only contributor review of the NexuML framework repository: a PR changes src/nexuml/core/compiler.py and .github/workflows/ci.yml. I want feedback on the framework's architecture and tests, not help using installed NexuML in an external user library. Identify relevant contributor files and a small review plan. Do not install NexuML, load the external-user agent skills, edit files or execute code.
evals.expected_output: Routes to ordinary repository contributor guidance, not skills for using an installed external NexuML library.
expectations: Does not load an installed-NexuML user skill merely because the framework name appears.
Distinguishes contributor source review from external library authoring or running a scenario.
Proposes source/test-specific review without inventing external library setup or training.

evals.name: novel-method-plus-experiments-overlap
evals.prompt: Read-only plan in my external installed-NexuML library: create a new prototype-guided differentiable loss, validate its gradients and TensorDict routing, then compare it with a matched existing baseline using three bounded validation-only ablations. Explain which NexuML procedural skills apply and give minimal implementation plus experiment gates. No code edits, training or final-test access.
evals.expected_output: Naturally routes to reusable algorithm authoring and bounded autoresearch, separating numerical correctness from controlled scientific comparison.
expectations: Selects both reusable component guidance and bounded research guidance without demanding a new all-in-one skill.
Requires a small numerical/gradient and route verification before running an ablation.
Preserves matched baseline/protocol/resource limits and final-test isolation.

evals.name: faithful-reference-then-novel-variant-overlap
evals.prompt: Read-only plan for a user-owned external NexuML library. First faithfully reproduce a published algorithm with official splits and metric, then investigate a separately named new loss under an explicit validation-only budget. Explain which guidance applies when and how to keep reference and improved method scientifically separate. No code or training.
evals.expected_output: Naturally routes to reproduction for reference fidelity and research for subsequent improvements, with library authoring when components are missing.
expectations: Starts with source-linked exact reproduction and a frozen reference baseline.
Preserves explicit assumptions and verified partition, metric and data identity.
Runs later improvements as separate hypotheses, only with research data and unchanged baselines.
